## Goal
The Pretext frontend (p.apyr.us today, Threat Intelligence later) reads article bodies from the stored Markus IR (`bodyIr`) instead of the `body: string[]` field, with a one-time command that converts existing `body[]` data. Result: one authored format everywhere (docs/standard-site.md 1.8). Clean break: no dual reading of `body[]`.

## Context (verified)
- `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts`: `GraphQLItem.body` (L77); `normalizeArticle` L633-661 returns `body: resolvedContent.body ?? compactStrings(item.body)` (L659); `normalizePublicationItem` L663-691 (L685 same); `resolveItemContentFromAttachments` L693-701 reads body text from a private S3 attachment pointer `editorial.attachments.body` (`parseContentAttachmentPointers` L717, `readAttachmentPointerText` L703, `textToParagraphs` L752) and the excerpt. Production p.apyr.us bodies may live in those attachments (`papyrus content backfill-item-body-attachments` / `scrub-item-inline-body` exist in `src/papyrus_content/item_content_commands.py`), not inline.
- Projection already exists: `lib/markus-projection.ts` `projectMarkusDocumentToPretext(doc) -> { body: string[], pullQuotes: string[], images: ArticleImageAsset[] }` and `lib/markus-ir.ts` `parseMarkusDocument(raw)` (throws on `schema_version` mismatch); `lib/markus-to-article.ts` uses them for the Pilobol sample. `lib/articles.ts` `Article.body: string[]` is the solver input and stays.
- `bodyIr` envelope: defined in `PPY-e169c5` (sentinel tokens `PAPYRUSMARKUP00001END` for `::image{}`, `[@key]`, `::citations{}`, resolved from `envelope.papyrus`).
- Python writers of `body[]`: `src/papyrus_content/seed_edition.py` `seed_article_records()` L270, L296 (`"body": article.get("body") or []`); `amplify/seed/seed.ts` `seedArticle` L495-790 (writes `body: []` plus S3 attachments L558+); legacy `scripts/content-cli.cjs` (L12641). Existing media lookup: `listMediaAssets(itemId)` and `normalizeImageAsset(item, asset)` L776.
- `docs/standard-site.md` 1.8: Pretext applies the projection to `bodyIr` at read time; legacy `body[]` removed after a one-time conversion; no compatibility shim.

## Exact changes
1. `lib/markus-body.ts` (new):
   ```ts
   export class BodyIrError extends Error {}
   export type BodyProjection = { body: string[]; pullQuotes: string[]; imageSrcs: Array<{ src: string; alt: string; caption?: string; credit?: string; layout?: string }>; };
   export function projectBodyIr(raw: unknown): BodyProjection
   ```
   `raw` is the AWSJSON value (string or object). Checks `schemaVersion === 1` and `markus.irSchemaVersion === 1` else throws `BodyIrError` (no fallback). `parseMarkusDocument(envelope.document)` then `projectMarkusDocumentToPretext`. Token post-processing on the projected `body[]`: a paragraph exactly equal to an image token is removed and its `papyrus.images[token]` appended to `imageSrcs` in order; `[@key]` tokens inside a paragraph are replaced by `[n]` numbered by first appearance (same order as `papyrus.bibliography`); a paragraph that is exactly a `citationLists` token is replaced by the `bibliography` strings (one paragraph each, prefixed `n. `).
2. `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts`: in `normalizeArticle` and `normalizePublicationItem` replace the body source by `projectBodyIr(item.bodyIr)`: `body = projection.body`, `pullQuotes = projection.pullQuotes` (drop `compactStrings(item.pullQuotes)`), images: each `imageSrcs[i]` matched to a media row by `JSON.parse(asset.metadata).srcPath === src` (external `http(s)` srcs become an `ArticleImageAsset` directly) and passed through `normalizeImageAsset`; media rows not referenced by the body are still included (cover images). Missing `bodyIr` on a published article/page -> throw `BodyIrError("PublishedItem <slug> has no bodyIr; run: papyrus content convert-bodies")`. Delete: `GraphQLItem.body`, `compactStrings(item.body)` uses for body, the BODY half of `resolveItemContentFromAttachments`/`readAttachmentPointerText`/`textToParagraphs` (keep the excerpt path).
3. `src/papyrus_content/convert_bodies_commands.py` (new) + CLI `papyrus content convert-bodies [--models Item,PublishedItem] [--dry-run] [--json]` (wire in `cli.py`): for each `Item`/`PublishedItem` of type `article` (or any type read by Pretext) with no `bodyMarkus`: resolve paragraphs = inline `body` if non-empty else the body attachment text (`model_attachments.download_attachment_buffer`, split on blank lines like `textToParagraphs`); `bodyMarkus = "

".join(escape_markdown(p) for p in paragraphs)` where `escape_markdown` backslash-escapes `\ ` * _ [ ] < > ~ |` everywhere and a leading `#`, `+`, `-`, `:`, or `\d+[.)]`; `fm = None`; `envelope = derive_body(None, bodyMarkus)`; VERIFY `plain_paragraphs(envelope) == [normalize_ws(p) for p in paragraphs]` (collapse whitespace) else skip the record and report it (no write); write `bodyMarkus`, `bodyIr` (`to_aws_json`), `metadata = {"convertedFrom": "body[]"}` via `update_record`. Does not touch `body`, `editorial` or attachments. Idempotent (records with `bodyMarkus` are skipped).
4. Seeds write the new shape: `seed_edition.py` `seed_article_records` writes `bodyMarkus`/`bodyIr` (via the same escape + `derive_body`) and no `body`; `amplify/seed/seed.ts`: remove article/edition/media seeding (keep users, groups, sections, doctrine, procedures); `npm run seed:amplify` docs (`amplify/seed/profiles/README.md`, `AGENTS.md` mentions) say articles are seeded with `poetry run papyrus content seed-edition`. (TS cannot derive the IR.)
5. Tests fixtures: `scripts/fixtures/body-ir/` envelopes generated from `PPY-e169c5` fixtures (`plain`, `image-and-citation`, `pull-quote`) via `papyrus content markus-derive --emit-ir` (commit the JSON).

## Data shapes
Output of `projectBodyIr` for `image-and-citation.md`: `body` = `["Intro with a claim [1].", "Second claim [1][2].", "1. Formatted APA string", "2. ..."]`, `imageSrcs = [{src:"images/a.png", alt:"A", layout:"full"}]`. Conversion example: `["Cats & dogs: *stars*", "# not a heading"]` -> `"Cats & dogs: \\*stars\\*

\\# not a heading"` and the verify step passes.

## Tests
- TS unit: `scripts/test-markus-body.ts` (npm script `test:markus-body`, `tsx`): the three fixtures project as above; wrong `schemaVersion` throws `BodyIrError`; token never leaks into output (`/PAPYRUSMARKUP/` absent); citation numbering order.
- Python unit: `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_convert_bodies.py` (`FakeAuthoringClient`): inline `body`, attachment-backed body (patch the download), escaping round-trip property over a list of nasty strings (`*`, `_`, `[x](y)`, `<b>`, `# h`, `1. x`, `---`, `|a|b|`, `:::x`, backticks, backslashes): `plain_paragraphs(derive(escape(p))) == [p]` for every case, and the command skips (reports) any case where it does not; idempotent re-run; `--dry-run` writes nothing.
- Existing: `scripts/test-markus-projection.ts`, `scripts/test-markus-to-article.ts` unchanged and green; `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- Gherkin (behave): `features_backend/convert-bodies.feature`: "Converting an article with a plain paragraph body preserves its text", "A paragraph that cannot be converted losslessly is reported and skipped". UI (cucumber): extend `features/` with `features/pretext-markus-body.feature` only if a demo route renders a scenario; otherwise cover with the TS unit test (do not add a UI feature without a demo fixture).
- Sandbox: seed with `poetry run papyrus content seed-edition`, run `npm run dev`, `curl -s localhost:3001/articles/<slug>` renders the body text from `bodyIr` (compare to the fixture JSON paragraph).

## Acceptance checks
- `npx tsx scripts/test-markus-body.ts`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_convert_bodies -v`, `poetry run behave features_backend/convert-bodies.feature` pass.
- Sandbox with legacy data (`body[]` only): `poetry run papyrus content convert-bodies --dry-run --json` lists every record as `convertible` or `skipped:<reason>`; after the real run the reader renders the same paragraphs (diff the visible text of 3 articles before/after: `curl -s .../articles/<slug> | sed -e 's/<[^>]*>//g'`).

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-44a0f9`, `PPY-e169c5`. Independent of `PPY-b3a10e`. Blocks the production promotion of anything that deploys the new reader (see risks). Same-file conflicts: `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` (also `PPY-3e5e9d`: land PRT first or coordinate; PRV adds a separate file and a small switch), `seed_edition.py` (helper move in `PPY-b3a10e`), `cli.py`.

## Risks
- OPERATIONAL ORDER (no shim means no overlap): production p.apyr.us (Papyrus `main`, Amplify app dbsyytcm9drqa) has `body[]` only. Sequence: (1) deploy `PPY-44a0f9` to production, (2) run `convert-bodies` against production (dry run first; Ryan approves, `AGENTS.local.md` for the profile), (3) only then promote the reader change to `main`. Until then keep this PR on `develop`. Threat Intelligence/Pilobol.us CMS deploys that float on Papyrus `main` follow the same gate.
- The `body` field stays in the schema until a Phase 4 cleanup ticket removes it (after step 2 is done everywhere).
- Removing TS article seeding changes the dev workflow (`ampx sandbox seed` no longer creates articles).
- Lossless conversion of paragraphs containing Markdown-significant characters is the point of the verify step; any skipped record needs a human look (list is printed).
- `bodyIr` size limit applies (`PPY-e169c5`); a converted long article that exceeds it is reported and skipped.

## Needs Ryan
Approval to run `convert-bodies` on production p.apyr.us (step 2) and to promote the reader to `main` afterwards.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-cddfb8-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
